newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil stable on firmer IPE.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil stable on firmer IPE.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps edged back up from a mid-afternoon low late Wednesday on a stronger IPE open, brokers said.
"The market gained some strength from the stronger IPE gas oil open," a trader said.
February gas oil swaps was last quoted at $28.60/$28.80 a barrel, against this morning's $28.90/$29.05. It hit an intra-day low of $28.55/$28.65, brokers said.
The market traded in the morning at between $28.78 and $28.92 a barrel and in the afternoon at $28.70, brokers said.
March traded twice at $28.43 a barrel and was last quoted at $28.40/$28.50, one broker said.
The February/March time spread narrowed to 20/30 cents from last week's 70/80 cents, reflecting the fundamental weakness of the market, traders said.
February gas oil futures on IPE was last traded firmer at 0945 GMT to $216 a tonne, up $2.25. The market closed down $5.25 a tonne to $213.75 on Tuesday.
The market remained slightly bearish as China was not buying while ample supplies were seen from several regional sources including Singapore and South Korea, one trader said.
Fuel oil was down with February last quoted at $112.50/$113.50 a tonne, from midday's $113.25/$114.50, brokers said.
